newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Britain and China agreed that 509 armed People's Liberation Army (PLA) soldiers and 39 vehicles would enter the territory three hours before the official handover ceremony at midnight on June 30.

-- All military staff on vacation have been called back to Beijing to strengthen security over the handover period. Several thousand police were transferred from the suburbs to the centre of the Chinese capital, with a total of 30,000 security staff now patrolling the streets.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Most Hong Kong people worry that the PLA garrison will enjoy privileges after the handover. A military expert said although rules prohibited PLA soldiers from doing business, the huge gap between their income and that of Hong Kong people might force the Chinese troops to resort to other means of making money.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Figures from the Futures and Securities Commission showed that in recent months, the number of new securities firms with mainland backing increased sharply. There were now 42 securities firms funded by China in Hong Kong, compared with only 28 at the end of March.

-- SING TAO -- As China's Communist Party prepares for its 15th general conference, a report is circulating in Beijing that says bourgeois ideology has permeated the media and all levels of party cadres. The report warns if the party ignores the bourgeois influence, its control over ideology will gradually be lost.

-- WEN WEI PO -- The first phase of the project to clean up the Shenzhen river on the border of the Chinese city of Shenzhen and Hong Kong will be completed ahead of schedule with an initial investment of HK$270 million (US$34.9 million).

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- One of Hong Kong's biggest property agents, Centaline Property Agency, called for a reduction in the amount banks were prepared to lend to property investors in a bid to curb speculation.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Beijing hailed success in bringing order to its troubled western province of Xinjiang, which was hit by riots and bombings. In the past six months, it said, more than 300 people had been arrested and 1,000 cases cleared up.
